increment_paragraph: **RULE35-PILOT** (pluggable-cards seam B, phase P2, the first pilot of GATEWAY-RULE-API-PILOT-MIGRATIONS; [report](../../reports/rule35-pilot/README.md)) moves gateway rule 35 out of `qcore-c-gateway` into the rule package `crates/gateway-rules/rule-35-literal-decay` (depends on the rule API only): the classification arm `literal-read` and the typed-reader arm `array-member-decay`, with their decision tables bound to `QCore.LiteralDecayReadings` (unchanged; the proof did not move). The rule API gains the host capabilities `LexicalHost` and `TypedHost`, the non-exhaustive `TypedReading` and the parity `Witness`, and `TypedReaderArm` becomes `reads`/`ask`/`witness`; the gateway hosts the package in `rule_hosts.rs` through the registry switch, refuses an admission carrying obligations, and keeps no rule-35 decision. The registry row names the package, and the generator refuses a crate that is not the gateway or a package under `crates/gateway-rules/`, or an arm route that is not a `pub fn` of it; a layering test holds every rule package to the API. One `quirin-audit measure` run (base `rev:80c8aea98`, tip `rev:555bd17db`, `--rules-off 35`, `--declared`, three live profiles, complete in 10 h 13 min): system and slice byte-identical, corpus 0 of 4,834 rows moved and equal under a checked one-to-one substitution of 64-hex digests and 24-hex contract ids (MEASURE-CORPUS-SIDE-CWD-IN-BUILD-IDENTITY), every profile reproducing its baseline; rule 35's switch-measured ledgers (`contract/contributions/35/`): eight-home 12 Unknown→Safe (exactly the rule card's twelve), system and slice 0 rows with leaf trades only; check and consistency pass. Parity cost: about 30 min to move the code, ten hours to measure.
status_paragraph: Gateway rule packages (2026-10-29, RULE35-PILOT): rule 35 is the first rule outside `qcore-c-gateway`, in `crates/gateway-rules/rule-35-literal-decay`, hosted through the rule API with no verdict change on the three live profiles, and its contribution is the first switch-measured ledger ([contributions](development/contributions.md)): eight-home 12 Unknown→Safe, system and slice no row. The other pilot rules' bodies still live in `qcore-c-gateway`.

ledger.text: RULE35-PILOT (2026-10-29) migrated rule 35 (identity run complete on all three live profiles; ledgers in contract/contributions/35/). It fixed the host capabilities the later pilots reuse: LexicalHost, TypedHost, the non-exhaustive TypedReading, Witness, and a reads/ask/witness TypedReaderArm; hosted arms refuse an admission with obligations (GATEWAY-RULE-API-ARM-OBLIGATIONS), which rule 37's premise needs first. Parity cost for plan decision 6: about 370 decision lines moved, 30 min of porting, 1 h 15 min active, 10 h 13 min measuring (three sides, three routes, under contention). Remaining: 37, 36, 33, 34, 32a.

DISCHARGE (RULE35-PILOT, 2026-10-29): one real `measure --rules-off 35` on a migrated rule completed (status complete, no failures, the post-run off-list check passed: tip-off components record off = ["35"], the other sides none); its contribution slot holds three quirin-contribution-ledger/1 ledgers built from the tip-off -> tip comparison, equal to rule 35's recorded delta (12 corpus rows), written with contribution_ledgers.py write and passing check and consistency.

ledger.text: Observed again by RULE35-PILOT (base rev:80c8aea98, tip rev:555bd17db): 365 components for 185 rows, 0 rows moved; besides 64-hex digests the moved build identity also moves 24-hex `resource_contracts:` ids and id-sorted evidence order, which GATEWAY-RULE-API's substitution.py cannot pair; docs/reports/rule35-pilot/scripts/substitution_ids.py checks a one-to-one substitution of both token kinds with lists as multisets (all five differing corpus artifacts pass). A fix in the tool would retire both checkers.

ledger.title: Production-source scans skip rule packages
ledger.text: Tests that enumerate production sources as `crates/*/src` (for example qcore-verification's composition_bounds.rs `production_sources`, the E03-B-O3 vacuity tripwire) do not see `crates/gateway-rules/<package>/src`, which RULE35-PILOT introduced. Rule 35's package states no such derivation, so nothing is missed today. DISCHARGE: every production-source scan includes rule packages, with a test naming rule 35's package.

ledger.title: Hosted arms cannot carry an admission's obligations
ledger.text: The gateway's rule host (`rule_hosts.rs`, RULE35-PILOT) refuses any arm admission that carries `Obligation::Premise` or `Obligation::Open`, because no arm placement has a row that could carry it (fail-closed, nothing dropped). Rule 37's `asserted_allocation` premise is the first that needs one. DISCHARGE: the position a premise-carrying arm answers at carries its obligations into the row's assumptions (and an open obligation into the denominator), with a test, before such an arm is hosted.
